import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    target_snapshot = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc_events = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    
    # Ensure proper dtypes
    target_snapshot["device_id"] = target_snapshot["device_id"].astype("int64")
    target_snapshot["reading"] = target_snapshot["reading"].astype("float64")
    target_snapshot["applied_event_ts"] = pd.to_datetime(target_snapshot["applied_event_ts"], utc=False)
    
    cdc_events["event_seq"] = cdc_events["event_seq"].astype("int64")
    cdc_events["event_ts"] = pd.to_datetime(cdc_events["event_ts"], utc=False)
    cdc_events["device_id"] = cdc_events["device_id"].astype("int64")
    cdc_events["reading"] = cdc_events["reading"].astype("float64")
    
    # Create a dict of current applied_event_ts per device
    watermark_map = dict(zip(target_snapshot["device_id"], target_snapshot["applied_event_ts"]))
    
    # Filter events: keep only those strictly greater than device watermark
    def passes_watermark(row):
        device_id = row["device_id"]
        event_ts = row["event_ts"]
        
        if device_id not in watermark_map:
            # New device: accept all events
            return True
        
        current_watermark = watermark_map[device_id]
        # Event must be strictly greater than watermark
        return event_ts > current_watermark
    
    cdc_events["passes_wm"] = cdc_events.apply(passes_watermark, axis=1)
    surviving_events = cdc_events[cdc_events["passes_wm"]].copy()
    surviving_events = surviving_events.drop(columns=["passes_wm"])
    
    # For each device, find the event with max (event_ts, event_seq)
    # Use stable sort to ensure deterministic tie-breaking
    if len(surviving_events) > 0:
        # Sort by device_id, then event_ts (desc), then event_seq (desc)
        surviving_events = surviving_events.sort_values(
            by=["device_id", "event_ts", "event_seq"],
            ascending=[True, False, False],
            kind="stable"
        )
        
        # Keep only the first (latest) event per device
        latest_per_device = surviving_events.drop_duplicates(subset=["device_id"], keep="first")
        
        # Create new rows from these events
        updated_rows = latest_per_device[["device_id", "reading", "event_ts"]].copy()
        updated_rows = updated_rows.rename(columns={"event_ts": "applied_event_ts"})
    else:
        updated_rows = pd.DataFrame(columns=["device_id", "reading", "applied_event_ts"])
    
    # Start with current snapshot
    new_snapshot = target_snapshot[["device_id", "reading", "applied_event_ts"]].copy()
    
    # Update devices that have surviving events
    if len(updated_rows) > 0:
        # Set index on device_id for efficient update
        updated_dict = dict(zip(updated_rows["device_id"], 
                               zip(updated_rows["reading"], updated_rows["applied_event_ts"])))
        
        for device_id, (new_reading, new_ts) in updated_dict.items():
            mask = new_snapshot["device_id"] == device_id
            if mask.any():
                new_snapshot.loc[mask, "reading"] = new_reading
                new_snapshot.loc[mask, "applied_event_ts"] = new_ts
            else:
                # New device: add row
                new_row = pd.DataFrame({
                    "device_id": [device_id],
                    "reading": [new_reading],
                    "applied_event_ts": [new_ts]
                })
                new_snapshot = pd.concat([new_snapshot, new_row], ignore_index=True)
    
    # Ensure proper dtypes in output
    new_snapshot["device_id"] = new_snapshot["device_id"].astype("int64")
    new_snapshot["reading"] = new_snapshot["reading"].astype("float64")
    new_snapshot["applied_event_ts"] = pd.to_datetime(new_snapshot["applied_event_ts"], utc=False)
    
    # Sort by device_id for deterministic output
    new_snapshot = new_snapshot.sort_values("device_id", ignore_index=True)
    
    return {"new_snapshot": new_snapshot}
